title: GWPTools: An extensible Wolfram Language framework for time-dependent Gaussian wave packet dynamics
authors: Jeremy B. Maddox, Ismail Giliani, Carter M. Heck, Connor S. Mattingly
abstract: Gaussian wave packets provide an exact analytical foundation for modeling time-dependent quantum phenomena, effectively bridging the gap between classical trajectories and full quantum mechanics. We introduce GWPTools, a highly extensible Wolfram Language framework designed to compute exact time-dependent Gaussian wave packet dynamics using a unified symbolic-numeric architecture. Built upon a robust ``parameter bus'' and polymorphic dispatch, the software serves as an interactive pedagogical tool for exploring quantum theory and an exact algebraic engine for rigorously benchmarking numerical grid-based and trajectory methodologies. Version 1.0.0 focuses on exact time evolution in driven one-dimensional quadratic potentials. Native extensions into quantum hydrodynamics and phase space representations enable exact energy decompositions, analytical Bohmian trajectories, and symbolic derivations of quasi-probability distributions and information metrics. We demonstrate the framework's modular scalability by prototyping interference in superpositions, open-system decoherence, and coupled two-dimensional oscillators. Ultimately, these capabilities establish a versatile foundation for maximizing the reach of exact analytical modeling toward increasingly complex driven quantum systems.
summary: This paper presents GWPTools, a specialized Wolfram Language framework designed to compute time-dependent Gaussian wave packet dynamics with high analytical rigor. It provides an exact symbolic-numeric engine to calculate key quantum diagnostics, such as quantum potential and entropy, for systems governed by quadratic potentials. The tool serves as both a pedagogical resource and a rigorous benchmark for validating various numerical simulation techniques in quantum physics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a robust, exact analytical framework to model complex time-dependent quantum phenomena, specifically bridging the gap between classical trajectories and full quantum mechanics.
main_result: The authors introduce GWPTools, an extensible Wolfram Language framework that provides an exact symbolic-numeric engine for calculating time-dependent Gaussian wave packet dynamics.
method: The framework uses the exact Gaussian ansatz and derives time evolution by solving coupled ODEs for the wave packet parameters, enabling exact calculation of expectation values and quantum diagnostics.
model_or_system: The model centers on time-dependent Gaussian wave packets (GWPs) governed by the Schrödinger equation, initially restricted to locally quadratic potentials $V(x, t) = V_0(t) + V_1(t)x + V_2(t)x^2$. It can be extended to handle various potentials and open-system dynamics.
key_observables: Position and momentum expectation values ($\langle x^n angle, \langle p^n angle$), quantum potential, Bohmian trajectories, Wigner function, and Wehrl entropy ($S_{Wehrl}$).
important_parameters: The core dynamics are governed by the time-dependent parameters ($\alpha_t, x_t, p_t, \gamma_t$) defining the Gaussian wave packet.
main_assumptions: Version 1.0.0 primarily assumes potentials are exactly quadratic for purely symbolic evaluation, although numerical extensions are provided for more complex potentials.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the GWPTools framework, details the mathematical machinery for exact derivative calculation and expectation values, and demonstrates its modular scalability by prototyping complex phenomena like decoherence and interference.
why_interesting: This tool provides a powerful, exact analytical benchmark for studying time-dependent quantum dynamics, which is crucial for validating numerical methods used in AMO physics and open quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Visual representation of the GWPObject summary boxes generated by the GWP constructor for varying input parameters. The frontend interface provides immediate access to the top-level state metadata, while the underlying data container stores the full 11-element parameter bus utilized by the polymorphic dispatcher.

Figure 2: A three-dimensional visualization of the exact spatio-temporal probability den- sity grid (data) generated for the freely dispersing Gaussian wave packet (OBJ3). Because the data is generated algebraically, the surface avoids the numerical accumulation errors typical of discretized time-evolution solvers.

Figure 3: Exact Bohmian trajectories overlaid on the time-dependent spatial probabil- ity density ρ(x, t). (a) Evolution of a Gaussian wave packet within a standard har- monic oscillator potential ("HO"), demonstrating periodic breathing and stable kinemat- ics. (b) Complex driven dynamics within a non-resonant forced harmonic oscillator ("NonResonantForcedHO"). In both cases, the hydrodynamic trajectories—corresponding to probability quantiles c ∈{1/10, 2/10, . . . , 9/10}—are generated algebraically by directly evaluating the exact inverse cumulative distribution function ("XC"). This analytical map- ping completely bypasses the need for numerical differential equation solvers,...

Figure 4: Exact analytical dynamics of superposition states within a harmonic oscillator potential. The panels illustrate a displaced coherent state wave packet colliding with a stationary ground-state wave packet. Panels (a) and (c) display the antisymmetric superposition, showcasing the persistent probability node at the origin during the collision event (t = π/2). Panels (b) and (d) display the symmetric superposition, demonstrating constructive interference at the collision center.

Figure 5: Exact propagation of a reduced density matrix simulating an open quantum sys- tem coupled to a harmonic environment. Panel (a) plots the time-dependent decoherence function, illustrating the continuous loss of quantum coherence as the system evolves. Panel (b) shows the exact spatio-temporal probability density ρ(x, t) overlaid with the position center parameter xt (solid line). The analytical evaluation captures the exact spatial broadening and environmental damping dictated by the Caldeira-Leggett master equation.
